items.quote: So the man of God interceded with the Lord
items.contrast: The king requests prayer, while the man of God performs it.
items.reason: The passage explicitly assigns the intercession to the man of God, not to the king who asks for help.

items.quote: The next day they let the cavalry go on with him, while they returned to the barracks.
items.contrast: The cavalry continue with Paul, while the other soldiers return to the barracks.
items.reason: The contrast within the sentence distinguishes the group allowed to continue from the soldiers referred to by “they,” who return.

items.quote: Uzziah rested with his ancestors and was buried near them in a cemetery that belonged to the kings, for people said, “He had leprosy.” And Jotham his son succeeded him as king.
items.contrast: Jotham’s succession follows the burial, whereas Isaiah’s recording of the reign is mentioned earlier.
items.reason: The narrative places Jotham succeeding Uzziah immediately after the account of Uzziah’s burial.

items.quote: From there they went on to the hill country of Ephraim and came to Micah’s house.
items.contrast: The hill country of Ephraim is the last named area before Micah’s house; Kiriath Jearim is an earlier stop.
items.reason: The route clearly supports the key, but “the residence the Danites visit” is an avoidable generic substitute for the explicitly named Micah’s house.

items.quote: the man of God is buried; lay my bones beside his bones. For the message he declared
items.contrast: The man of God originally declared the message, while the current speaker says that it will come true.
items.reason: The window supports the intended answer through the antecedent of “he,” but the question blurs the original declarer with the current speaker. Asking who originally declared the message would recover the intended relation.
